# System Design from Scratch

> A free, open-source curriculum that builds system design mechanisms in Go,
> measures their trade-offs, and grades design judgement against rubrics.
> No claim without a number the lesson produced.

Generated 2026-09-11. 1 of 49 planned lessons written.

## Lesson types

- Build: a real algorithm implemented in Go with tests that assert the trade-off
- Simulate: a measurable experiment for systems too large to build in a lesson
- Design: a brief with a self-scoring rubric, traps, and a reference direction

## Curriculum

### Foundations

The vocabulary and the arithmetic. What the properties mean, what they cost, and the primitives that show up in every later phase.

- Why System Design Is a Separate Skill (design) — planned, not yet written
- Back-of-Envelope Estimation (build) — planned, not yet written
- [Consistent Hashing](https://systemdesignfromscratch.com/lesson?id=01-foundations/03-consistent-hashing) (build)
  Adding one server to a modulo-hashed cache moves 81% of your keys. A hash ring moves 20%. Same hardware, same request, one line of different arithmetic.
- Rate Limiting: Token Bucket to Sliding Window (build) — planned, not yet written
- Caching Strategies and Eviction (build) — planned, not yet written
- Backpressure and Load Shedding (build) — planned, not yet written
- Circuit Breakers (build) — planned, not yet written
- Bloom Filters (build) — planned, not yet written
- Why p99 Is Not an Average (simulate) — planned, not yet written

### Networking and Routing

How a request finds a server, and what happens when the server it finds is the wrong one.

- Load Balancing: Round Robin to Power of Two Choices (build) — planned, not yet written
- Health Checks and Outlier Detection (build) — planned, not yet written
- Service Discovery (build) — planned, not yet written
- Stateless Service Design (design) — planned, not yet written
- Retries, Timeouts and Deadline Propagation (build) — planned, not yet written
- CDNs and Edge Caching (simulate) — planned, not yet written

### Data and Storage

Where state lives, how it survives a crash, and what you give up to make it fast.

- Write-Ahead Logs (build) — planned, not yet written
- B-Trees versus LSM Trees (build) — planned, not yet written
- Indexes and Query Cost (simulate) — planned, not yet written
- Replication and Replica Lag (simulate) — planned, not yet written
- Partitioning and Rebalancing (build) — planned, not yet written
- Transactions and Isolation Levels (build) — planned, not yet written
- Choosing a Datastore (design) — planned, not yet written

### Distributed Systems

What breaks once one machine becomes several, and the algorithms that make disagreement survivable.

- How Distributed Systems Actually Fail (simulate) — planned, not yet written
- Logical and Vector Clocks (build) — planned, not yet written
- Quorums and Tunable Consistency (build) — planned, not yet written
- Leader Election (build) — planned, not yet written
- Raft: Log Replication from Scratch (build) — planned, not yet written
- Gossip Protocols (build) — planned, not yet written
- Merkle Trees and Anti-Entropy (build) — planned, not yet written
- CAP Beyond the Triangle (design) — planned, not yet written

### Messaging and Streams

Decoupling components in time, and the delivery guarantees you can actually buy.

- Queues versus Append-Only Logs (build) — planned, not yet written
- At-Most-Once, At-Least-Once, Exactly-Once (build) — planned, not yet written
- Idempotency Keys and Deduplication (build) — planned, not yet written

- Consumer Groups and Partition Assignment (build) — planned, not yet written
- Windowing and Late Data (simulate) — planned, not yet written

### Operating in Production

The properties you only discover after launch: observability, cost, and the failure you did not plan for.

- Metrics, Logs and Traces (build) — planned, not yet written
- SLOs and Error Budgets (build) — planned, not yet written
- Capacity Planning and Cost Modelling (simulate) — planned, not yet written

### Real-World Systems

Full designs where constraints conflict and something has to give. Each one names what it sacrifices.
